Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Consistent assessment findings:
  - Acute asthma exacerbation suspected, with wheeze and dyspnea on exertion; history of childhood asthma; previous albuterol use; possible triggers include viral infection or allergen exposure
  - Recent fever (37°C) and cough, suggesting a possible viral trigger contributing to airway inflammation
  - No nocturnal symptoms reported; patient able to walk/perform some activity; current limitation with speaking at times
- Differential diagnoses (see Summary of Differential Diagnoses section)

Management Plan
- Increase short-acting beta-agonist (albuterol/salbutamol) use; advise more regular use
  - Recommend 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially
  - Spacer: advised; not currently available at home; spacer prescription discussed
  - Peak flow meter: prescription offered to monitor breathing
- Monitoring and follow-up
  - Arrange a review in about 1 week to assess asthma control and consider initiation of controller therapy
  - If fever worsens or wheeze worsens, patient to contact back promptly
  - Record peak flow values (morning and evening) for the next week; discuss results by phone
- Additional therapies
  - Regular antihistamine to manage hay fever (pharmacy prescription recommended)
- Education and self-management
  - Pharmacist to provide instruction on spacer use and peak flow meter use
  - Discuss potential triggers (viral/infection, allergens) and activity adjustments during flare

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute asthma exacerbation — High
  - Justification: History of childhood asthma; current wheeze and dyspnea; prior inhaler use; clinician’s framing as an asthma flare; potential triggers include viral infection or allergen exposure
- Viral upper respiratory infection triggering bronchospasm — Moderate
  - Justification: Fever and cough; possible viral trigger for airway reactivity
- Allergic asthma/allergic rhinitis interplay — Moderate
  - Justification: History of hay fever; atopy-consistent airway hyperreactivity
- Acute bronchitis — Moderate
  - Justification: Cough with airway inflammation; could coexist with or precipitate asthma flare; lack of sputum production or imaging data limits certainty
